blocks.text: El Chaltén, Argentina: peaks and a glacier reflected in the still waters of a lake
El Chaltén to Puerto Natales, Chile

Transfer to Puerto Natales. The road crosses mountain terrain and the Patagonian steppe. Along the way, you may spot llamas, hares, foxes and alpacas.

After crossing the border, arrive in Puerto Natales and check in.
Puerto Natales to Torres del Paine

After breakfast, set out on a full-day excursion to Torres del Paine National Park.

The park's granite towers rise almost vertically more than 2,000 metres above the Patagonian steppe. Before the park was established in 1959, the area was used as an extensive sheep pasture. Its ecosystems took a long time to recover from intensive grazing.

The park is now part of UNESCO's biosphere reserve network. It contains blue and emerald lakes, forests, fast-flowing rivers, waterfalls, footbridges and glaciers. Wildlife includes rheas, Andean condors, flamingos and guanacos.

Guanacos graze on the open steppe, where predators have a harder time approaching unseen. After years of protection from poaching, large herds are accustomed to people and vehicles.

The itinerary includes the Mylodon Cave on Cerro Benítez, about 25 km from Puerto Natales. Remains of a sabre-toothed cat, an American horse and a large prehistoric sloth were found here in 1895. The cave takes its name from Darwin's ground sloth, which lived in the region 8,000–10,000 years ago. A sculpture of the animal stands at the entrance.

The park covers more than 242,000 hectares. The landscape shifts from lakes and granite mountains to waterfalls and glaciers.

A walk of about 15 minutes leads to Salto Grande waterfall, which connects Lakes Nordenskjöld and Pehoé. On the return journey, pass the Serrano River and Lakes Toro and Porteño. Return to Puerto Natales and spend the night at the hotel.
